system:
Write investigate(context, acquire) in ordinary restricted Python.
Put the COMPLETE EXECUTABLE PYTHON PROGRAM in the JSON source field. Include
the function definition and body, never a label, description or bare signature.
The scope and lesson fields contain short technical claims.
context has source_id, actions, goal and documentation. acquire("history") returns
all calibration receipts for this source. Use no case identifiers, private data,
external tools or imports. Infer behavior from the actual observations and public
documentation; generalize to new action combinations and values. Return exactly
{"value": integer or null, "unresolved": boolean}. Do not merely memorize probe
outputs. Resolve a goal only when the evidence supports it; source identity binds
the evidence, it does not explain behavior. scope and lesson are short technical
claims, not a chain-of-thought transcript.

Only function definitions at module level. No imports, annotations, decorators,
default arguments, private names, exceptions, while loops, I/O or global state.
For loops, comprehensions, lambda, nonlocal closure variables, del of local
names or container entries, and arithmetic except power are permitted.
Builtins: abs all any bool dict enumerate float int isinstance len list max min
range reversed round set sorted str sum tuple zip.
Methods: get items keys values append extend sort lower upper strip split
setdefault add discard copy count index pop remove clear update.
At most eight acquisitions per query. Source limit 60000 UTF8 bytes. Programs
run in a fresh resource-limited process. Emit one JSON object, never an array.

prompt.documentation:
Predict a disposable SQLite source from its past measured experiments.
Each experiment starts with an empty items table (text primary key, nonnegative
integer value) and fresh main/other database connections. No state carries between
experiments. Actions are JSON dictionaries: put(key,value), update(key,value),
delete(key), begin, commit, rollback. Use the field op for the action name; an
optional connection is main (default) or other. Put submits an insertion with the
source's stable conflict handling; update changes an existing item's value;
delete removes an item. Values are integers 0..1000000 and keys are nonempty text
up to 40 characters. At most 32 actions are permitted. Transactions cannot nest.
While a transaction is open, writes and transaction actions use that connection;
the other connection can write after commit or rollback. A sequence may end with
an open transaction. A separate read connection measures committed state.

The source belongs to this disclosed, fixed 18-member family. Its put operation
uses exactly one of SQLite INSERT OR IGNORE, INSERT OR REPLACE, or INSERT with
ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE of the value. Instrumentation is either absent or one
AFTER INSERT trigger that inserts exactly one row into an otherwise unread
auxiliary log; there are no other triggers. Its channel is exactly one of:
main connection changes() (last direct row-change count), main total_changes,
or main total_changes plus other total_changes. Each combination is possible.
The actual combination is private and stable for this source. Infer it from
measurements, using native SQLite semantics; do not assume a counter measures
net committed effects. Calibration history gives actions, emitted channel and
independently read committed item count/value sum.

A query supplies a fresh action sequence and one goal: channel (the source's
emitted number), committed_count (items visible to the separate committed-state
reader), or committed_sum (sum of their values, zero when empty). Query contexts
contain no outcome for the requested sequence. Return value as an integer and
unresolved=false when the calibration evidence supports that answer, otherwise
value=null and unresolved=true. A value is supported exactly when every member
of the disclosed family consistent with all calibration receipts predicts that
same value for this goal and sequence. Otherwise it is unresolved; an unsupported
lucky guess is not a supported answer. Author your own executable predictor;
no candidate programs, simulator or solver library are supplied.

champion.lesson: The prior simulator's transaction model was wrong: it treated uncommitted writes as visible to the other connection and never discarded them on rollback. The corrected model keeps per-connection pending writes, applies them to the shared committed state only on commit, discards them on rollback, and treats an open transaction at the end as uncommitted. It also correctly counts changes() as the last statement's direct row changes, total_changes as cumulative direct changes, and the combined channel as main plus other total_changes, with the AFTER INSERT trigger adding one log row per successful insert.
champion.scope: Predicts channel, committed_count, and committed_sum for any action sequence over the disclosed 18-member family, using calibration receipts to identify the source's put mode, trigger presence, and channel definition.

prompt.request: Author a complete reusable observation program. Use the measured errors to change the computation, including coupled changes when necessary. A correct calibration score alone does not establish a correct model of new compositions. Preserve uncertainty where evidence cannot determine a goal.

proposal.lesson: The channel is main total_changes plus other total_changes, and the put operation is INSERT OR REPLACE. The trigger is absent. The channel counts every row change including ignored inserts, updates, deletes, and trigger inserts. The committed state is the final visible state after all actions, with uncommitted transactions rolled back.
proposal.scope: Predicts channel, committed_count, and committed_sum for any action sequence over the disclosed 18-member family, using calibration receipts to identify the source's put mode, trigger presence, and channel definition.

proposal.lesson: The prior simulator mishandled transaction semantics: it kept uncommitted writes in the visible state and never rolled them back, and it treated the two connections as sharing one table rather than as separate connections to the same database. The corrected model tracks per-connection pending writes, applies them to the shared committed state only on commit, discards them on rollback, and treats an open transaction at the end as uncommitted. It also correctly counts changes() as the last statement's direct row changes, total_changes as cumulative direct changes, and the combined channel as main plus other total_changes, with the AFTER INSERT trigger adding one log row per successful insert.
proposal.scope: Predicts channel, committed_count, and committed_sum for any action sequence over the disclosed 18-member family, using calibration receipts to identify the source's put mode, trigger presence, and channel definition.
